articles.headline: OFAC Issues International Criminal Court Designation and General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a new designation related to the International Criminal Court (ICC) on October 9, 2026. This action is accompanied by the issuance of new General Licenses.
Further details regarding the specific individuals or entities designated, and the scope of the associated General Licenses, are available through the official OFAC publication.
This move by OFAC signifies continued U.S. attention to the activities of the ICC and its personnel, potentially impacting those involved in or supporting its operations.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Burma-related Designation
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the removal of a Burma-related designation on October 9, 2026. This action indicates a change in the U.S. sanctions posture concerning the designated entity or individual.
Designation removals typically occur when the designated party is deemed to no longer meet the criteria for sanctions, or when there are policy shifts.
The specifics of the removed designation are detailed in the official OFAC publication, providing clarity on the entity no longer subject to U.S. sanctions under this program.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a new Russia-related General License on October 9, 2026. This license authorizes certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under the extensive Russia sanctions program.

General Licenses are often issued to provide carve-outs for specific activities, such as humanitarian aid, certain financial transactions, or the wind-down of operations, to mitigate unintended consequences of sanctions.

The precise scope and conditions of this new General License are outlined in the official OFAC publication, and parties engaging in Russia-related activities should review it carefully for applicability.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces New Iran-related Designations and General License
body: On October 8, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations, expanding the list of individuals and entities subject to U.S. sanctions.
Concurrently, OFAC issued a new Iran-related General License, which may authorize certain transactions or activities that would otherwise be prohibited under the comprehensive Iran sanctions program.
These actions underscore the U.S. government's continued pressure on Iran through economic sanctions, while also providing specific exemptions where deemed necessary for policy reasons.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Russia-related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Russia-related General License on October 8, 2026. Amendments to existing General Licenses often clarify, expand, or restrict the scope of previously authorized activities.
Such changes are typically made in response to evolving geopolitical circumstances, feedback from the private sector, or to fine-tune the impact of sanctions.
Entities engaged in transactions involving Russia should review the amended General License to ensure ongoing compliance with U.S. sanctions regulations.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Designations Removals and Updates, Publishes Iran-related Alert and FAQ
body: On October 5, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced several designations removals and updates, indicating adjustments to its various sanctions lists.

In addition, OFAC published an Iran-related Alert and an Amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ). These publications provide guidance and highlight specific risks or compliance considerations related to Iran sanctions.
The alert and FAQ are crucial resources for individuals and entities operating in or with connections to Iran, offering insights into OFAC's current enforcement priorities and interpretations.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Counter Terrorism Designations on October 2, 2026. These designations target individuals and entities identified as supporting or engaging in terrorist activities.
Such actions aim to disrupt the financial networks of terrorist organizations and prevent them from accessing the U.S. financial system.
The specific details of these designations, including the names of the designated parties, are available in the official OFAC publication.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Iran-related Designations, Transnational Criminal Organization Designation, and New Guidance
body: On October 1, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and designations updates, further tightening sanctions against entities and individuals connected to Iran.
Concurrently, OFAC designated a Transnational Criminal Organization (TCO) and published an Iran-related Determination and an Amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ).
These actions reflect a multi-pronged approach to address threats emanating from Iran and global criminal networks, providing both new restrictions and clarifying guidance for compliance.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organization Designations; Removes Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya Designations
body: On September 30, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations under its Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations programs, targeting entities and individuals involved in these illicit activities.
Simultaneously, OFAC removed several designations related to Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya, indicating a recalibration of sanctions in these areas.
These actions demonstrate OFAC's dynamic approach to sanctions, adding pressure where new threats emerge while adjusting existing measures as circumstances change.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces New Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran-related, and Non-Proliferation Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a broad set of new designations on September 29, 2026, targeting individuals and entities across multiple sanctions programs.
These designations fall under Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran-related, and Non-Proliferation authorities, highlighting a concerted effort to combat various illicit activities.

The comprehensive nature of these designations underscores the U.S. government's commitment to disrupting networks involved in drug trafficking, terrorism financing, proliferation of weapons, and supporting the Iranian regime.

articles.headline: OFAC Publishes Regulatory Amendments, Cuba Sanctions Regulations, New FAQs, and Alert
body: On September 29, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) published significant regulatory amendments, including updated Cuba Sanctions Regulations.
Accompanying these updates, OFAC issued new and amended Cuba-related Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) and a Cuba-related OFAC Alert.

These comprehensive publications provide critical guidance and clarifications for individuals and entities engaging in activities related to Cuba, reflecting ongoing adjustments to U.S. policy towards the island nation.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Venezuela General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Venezuela General Licenses on September 28, 2026. These amendments modify existing authorizations for certain transactions involving Venezuela.

Changes to General Licenses can impact a wide range of sectors, including oil, gas, and financial services, and are often a response to political developments or humanitarian considerations in Venezuela.
Parties operating under existing Venezuela General Licenses should carefully review the amended versions to ensure continued compliance and understand any new restrictions or allowances.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
